summary.headline: Sarda Energy Q1 FY27 total income INR 1,717 cr, EBITDA INR 762 cr and PAT INR 478 cr (+9.4% YoY), helped by a one-time INR 110 cr net benefit.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly EBITDA and PAT despite planned shutdowns, unplanned outages and weak small-hydro generation from delayed monsoon. Net profit included a one-time net benefit of INR 110 cr from regulatory approval of the final project cost of the 113 MW Sikkim hydro plant, which management said was worth about INR 162.6 cr of revenue and INR 18 cr of interest income. Energy contributed nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA, and the company said it is now net debt-free with liquidity above INR 2,500 cr as of 30 June 2026. Metals volumes fell QoQ because of captive power and furnace shutdowns at Raipur, Vizag and Siltara. Management declined to give numerical FY27 guidance.

segments.name: Energy (IPP and captive power)
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA. Medium and long-term PPAs cover over 380 MW of 710 MW saleable capacity; about 330 MW of these are at SKS, at INR 5-6/unit. Small hydro output was hit by the delayed monsoon, and the company said it is roughly 1% below last year.

segments.name: Sikkim 113 MW hydro
segments.commentary: Shut from 18 June to 5 July 2026 after a transmission tower collapsed in heavy rain and landslide. Management said it is now running at full capacity, with about 5 days of July generation lost and the restoration cost covered by insurance apart from a minimal excess.

segments.name: Steel and ferro alloys (metals)
segments.commentary: Consolidated revenue fell QoQ on planned outages: a 30 MW captive unit replacement at Raipur (trial run now, commercial operation expected mid-August), a 23-day Vizag captive shutdown, and a 53-day Siltara ferro alloy furnace refurbishment. Steel prices were range-bound with a mild negative bias; ferro alloy prices improved modestly.

segments.name: Mineral wool (new)
segments.commentary: Running at about 60-65% of capacity, with production constrained by imported equipment held up by the West Asia crisis. Management said the project is not yet profitable, and it expects FY27 revenue of INR 90-110 cr.

segments.name: Mining (coal)
segments.commentary: Shahpur West is due to commission before end-FY27 (0.6 Mt). Bartunga Hill (2.1 Mt) is due by end-FY28. Gare Palma IV/5 (2.0 Mt), Gare Palma IV/7 (1.8 Mt) and Senduri (0.6 Mt, provisional) make up the mining plan; the target is 7.1 Mt capacity.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 PAT or EBITDA guidance; management said the company does not give forward profitability figures and that the market is volatile.
Q2 expected to be better than Q1, driven by hydro generation and higher power prices. July IEX prices were about INR 5/unit versus INR 4.19-4.20 a year earlier.
FY27 IPP generation expected to exceed last year's 415 crore units, with the captive plant utilisation also improving after the 30 MW unit restarts.
Steel and ferro alloy prices expected to remain stable. Ferro alloy margins may firm as raw material prices soften; steel may rise after a West Asia settlement and after monsoon.
Real power tariffs expected at INR 5-6/unit for the year, rising with inflation and peak demand, especially for hydro.

Full-year FY27 pipeline: 50 MW captive solar expected by end of next quarter (after a railway right-of-way delay); 74 MW Chhattisgarh small hydro approvals on schedule; Arunachal 66 MW hydro detailed engineering to begin this year.

SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW expansion: TOR submission in about 3 months, then public hearing and 6-8 months for EC, then 6-8 months to appoint a consultant. The new unit is targeted for FY31 completion (per management, asked on the last call).
capex_capacity: SKS thermal expansion from 600 MW to 1,200 MW is awaiting regulatory approval, and the company describes the brownfield project as capital-efficient, using existing land, water and evacuation infrastructure.
Waste heat recovery power plant at Vizag, about INR 300 cr, for energy efficiency; all expansion projects funded through internal accruals.

Coal mining: Shahpur West commissioning before end-FY27; Bartunga Hill by end of next financial year; Gare Palma IV/5, IV/7 and Senduri approvals in progress. Management said the Gare Palma IV/7 expansion from 1.8 Mt to 5 Mt is not in the immediate plan as new higher-grade mines take priority.
Shahpur West coal is high grade and is destined for sponge iron and ferro alloy plants, not the power plants.
Plans to quadruple mining capacity and double energy generation capacity, per management.
demand_pricing: India power generation grew 9.4% YoY to about 523 BU in the quarter; thermal grew 7.5%; solar generation rose about 45%; small hydro fell about 30% and large hydro about 7%.
Day-ahead market averaged INR 3.85/unit vs INR 3.92 a year earlier, but July prices rose to about INR 5/unit from INR 4.19. Management said peak hours have lengthened from 5 to 8-10 hours.
Indian coal index for June 2026 was about 21% above June 2025 and about 11% above March 2026.
India crude steel output grew over 7.5% in H1 CY26; imports exceeded exports again after two quarters. Management welcomed anti-dumping investigations.
West Asia conflict is raising input costs and creating supply chain issues. Management called the impact manageable but is in a wait-and-watch stance.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever quarterly EBITDA per management

financial_highlights.metric: One-time net benefit in PAT (Sikkim final project cost approval)
financial_highlights.change: Approx. INR 162.6 cr revenue and INR 18 cr other income pre-tax; about 25% of INR 110 cr at EBITDA level per CFO

financial_highlights.value: More than INR 2,500 cr as of 30 June 2026

qa_highlights.question: Is realisation per unit falling as more PPAs are signed, given the implied ~INR 8/unit on power sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the back-calculated realisation is wrong because current income includes prior-year adjustments. Full-year power should be assumed at INR 5-6/unit, rising with inflation and peak demand, especially for hydro.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 110 cr one-time benefit's P&L split available, and what is the other-income effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue impact was about INR 162.64 cr and other income about INR 18 cr (interest awarded with tariff). EBITDA effect is about 25% of the INR 110 cr, net of tax.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 380 MW of PPAs is at SKS, what tariff applies, and what is the maximum SKS PPA quantity?
qa_highlights.answer: About 330 MW of the 380 MW is at SKS, at INR 5-6/unit. Maximum SKS quantity is 540 MW, and management said it still has to decide how far to commit.

qa_highlights.question: Which coal mines make up the 7.1 Mt target, and is Gare Palma IV/7 expansion to 5 Mt planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gare Palma IV/7 is 1.8 Mt, Shahpur West 0.6 Mt, Senduri about 0.6 Mt (provisional), and Gare Palma IV/5 about 2.0 Mt. Management said the 1.8 to 5 Mt expansion is not in the immediate plan as new higher-grade mines take priority.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW environmental clearance timeline and construction start?
qa_highlights.answer: TOR submission in about 3 months, then public hearing and 6-8 months for EC, then 6-8 months to appoint a consultant before procedures start. Management did not give a construction start date.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new SKS unit be completed, and will turnover more than double?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated completion by FY31, as stated on the last call. On turnover doubling, management said it should be by that time.

qa_highlights.question: Has Sikkim hydro normalised, and is there residual Q2 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Sikkim is operating at full capacity. Management does not expect a residual impact in Q2, apart from about 5 days of July generation lost.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 PAT and EBITDA be guided numerically?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it does not give forward profitability guidance given the volatile market. It said Q2 should be better on hydro and July power prices, and FY27 IPP generation should exceed last year's 415 crore units.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mineral wool revenue, and what are the Q2 and FY27 sales and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant is at 60-65% of capacity and not yet profitable. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 90-110 cr, said Q2 is hard to comment on, and expects full production in about 6 months.

risks_watch: Delayed monsoon and hydro generation: small hydro was about 1% below last year in Q1, and Q2 depends on rainfall.
Mineral wool ramp-up: capacity at 60-65%, with imported equipment stuck due to the West Asia crisis; the project is loss-making.

Regulatory timing: SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW EC needs TOR, public hearing and 6-8 months; Arunachal and Chhattisgarh approvals and 50 MW solar commissioning depend on railway right-of-way (1-2 months expected).
Coal mine ramp-up: Shahpur West due before end-FY27, Bartunga Hill by end-FY28; Gare Palma IV/7 expansion not in immediate plan.
West Asia conflict: input cost inflation and supply chain disruption; steel prices hinge on a settlement. Solar daytime oversupply could weigh on day-time power prices, with BESS expected to offset.
Quality of earnings: Q1 PAT included a one-time INR 110 cr net benefit, and the company gave no numerical FY27 guidance.
key_quotes: Q1 FY '27 stands as testament to the series of decisions we have taken over the last few years to build a diversified integrated business model, one that has continued to help us navigate external challenges.

We are now net debt -free on both a stand -alone and consolidated basis with a strong balance sheet and healthy liquidity of more than INR 2,500 crores as of 30th June 2026, giving us significant flexibility to execute our long-term growth plans.
Generally, we don't give any forward guidance.
So giving any guidance on the specific numbers is not advisable.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and balance sheet (net debt-free, liquidity above INR 2,500 cr), but cautious and evasive on forward profitability, declining to give any numerical FY27 PAT or EBITDA guidance. Answers on the one-time benefit and the mineral wool timeline were more specific, while the mineral wool revenue and Q2 questions were answered with caveats.
